_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Roof and facade detail in the building spec
tasks.notes: Cause: the building spec has no vocabulary for roof or facade detail and feature_build places none. rules/building-review.md already asks the designer to list roof greeblies per roof from the aerial (plant boxes, vents, louvred vents, skylights, solar panels, lift overruns, parapets) and names a --greeblies feature follow-up step, but no script or lib has --greeblies (probably lost in the move from the Refine donor; not confirmed). Covers issue I-006 (no roof or facade detail), snags S-009 and S-016. Owner decision (2026-10-27): detail lives in the building spec, not a separate pass, so undo/redo of a building takes its detail with it. Scope: a per-label details table in the spec, each entry a kind, position and size: roof (plant room, vent, louvred vent, skylight, solar panel, lift overrun), facade (drainpipe, sign, canopy, ledge, fascia band); a small block recipe per kind in feature_build, placed after the shell; positions from the aerial (roofs) and street photos (facades), heights of large roof plant from lidar; the designer brief points at building-review and fills details; replace the dead --greeblies reference in the rules with the table; dry run prints each detail and its source. Done when a dry run of SUSU, West or Retail places listed roof and facade details, including Retail's entrance canopy (in its spec notes, never built). Check line S-009, S-016: each building in 48,-44 shows the roof plant and facade detail visible on the aerial and photos. Size l: may split into roof detail and facade detail. Blocked by #125 and #126: details sit on the roofs, and all touch feature_build.py. One regression test per part; no new gates or lints. UPDATE 2026-10-27: build on the per-face facade plan from #145 rather than a second spec table (hence blocked by it). Split: #145 owns entrances and the covered area or canopy over them; this task owns greeblies (roof and facade detail) and does not re-define canopy. Roof detail on stair-and-slab roofs follows #149.

tasks.title: Rebuild fixtures for undo tests
tasks.notes: Cause: undo tests hand-roll stage and modifies setup, and missed rebuilds of a layer over itself until the #123 check refused a real ground undo (2026-10-27, Highfield 48,-44). Deliver one test helper in journal_testkit that sets up a ghost base plus N rebuilds of a layer (same, wider, narrower), so undo tests cover rebuilt layers without per-test setup. Known traps: 'ghost-ground' is not an apply stage (use other), and a later build must list the base in modifies. Also covers the interleaved-build case the check refuses today (fails closed, documented in _before_footprints). Add a property test: apply N rebuilds of a layer with NO base owner underneath, then undo them all; the world must equal the start. (A bent fixture in the 2026-10-27 undo-check fix hid exactly this.)

tasks.title: Undo a whole cell in order
tasks.notes: Cause: purging a cell was done by hand and ran undo passes in the wrong order (ground before features); a refusal then halted the chain. Deliver one element_undo command that undoes everything above ghost in a cell in the fixed order (decor, trees, features, ground), stops at the first refusal and reports what is left. Dry run by default, --apply to write, under the site lock.

tasks.title: Purge scope: everything above ghost
tasks.notes: Cause: the purge skill offers element, cell and project, so 'purge the non-ghost stuff' was first read as the project reset, which also wipes ghost. Add a fourth scope to the purge skill: count from the new cells view, undo cell by cell with the new whole-cell command, then retire records and prove each cell is ghost only.

tasks.title: Status pages and morning report show unbuilt footprint per cell
tasks.notes: Cause: morning and site_pages called 48,-45 and 49,-45 complete when about half of 49,-45 was still empty footprint. Deliver: each cell row and the morning report show built vs unbuilt footprint area and the names of unbuilt buildings; a cell with unbuilt footprint cannot show as Completed.

tasks.title: Feature doors land in a one-block vestibule that patrol flags door_to_wall
tasks.notes: Cause: feature_build lays storey floors every 3 blocks from a median-ground level but places each door on its own wall column's lidar ground, so the door's inside cell is floor or solid; 6 flags in the world after 2026-10-27 (jubilee 1, susu 3, west 2). Doors also fall back to one leaf when no pair cell is free (42-B, 57-A, 40-A/B, 18-A). Deliver: tie storey floors to local ground at each door, or clear the inside cell; then a re-apply of the three specs gives 0 patrol flags and keeps two-leaf doors where the spec asks for them. UPDATE 2026-10-27: this is the old door path that #146 removes, and #145 plans floor height against outside ground (the sunk 42-B door, I-017). Do not fix it twice: #146 absorbs the work, and this task is the acceptance check afterwards (re-apply the three specs: 0 patrol door_to_wall flags, two-leaf doors where the plan says double). Close it if #146 already gives that.

tasks.title: Facade plan with entrances: the designer accounts for every portal
tasks.notes: Cause: doors are placed at the wall cell nearest a portal point (portals.framed, DOOR_REACH, #114) and the spec's optional `doors` map is rarely filled, so leaf count, face, canopy and floor height are guessed per door (S-021 sunk 42-B door, S-023 57-A on the wrong face, 40-A single not double). Deliver: a per-face facade plan in the building spec (storeys, glazing, entrances with leaf count, canopy or covered area, steps, floor height against outside ground; room for roof edge and detail). Portals are inputs to it, not a stage: the designer brief shows every portal on the footprint with its photo and position when it has one, and each must be placed or declared unresolved with a reason. Each entrance records its source (given coordinate or register entry, photo read, inference) and confidence. Portals are best effort: a world with no portal register still gets entrances from street-level photos. Relates to #130 (windows on every face), #131 (window frames) and #132 (roof and facade detail): decide whether they become fields of this plan or follow it. Check: 57-A is a single door on the side face under a covered area; 40-A shows double doors; 42-B sits at ground level; a portal left unresolved is listed in the plan and the cell view.

tasks.title: Build reads the facade plan; remove the old portal door path everywhere
tasks.notes: Deliver: feature doors and entrances are built from the facade plan (#145) only. Cleanup is part of the task, not a follow-up: remove the nearest-wall-cell door chooser (feature_build.py framed / DOOR_REACH), the legacy front/rear spruce default, the per-portal `doors` map and its spec docs, and scripts/door_audit.py's assumptions about them; keep scripts/portals.py and the register as an evidence reader feeding the designer. Update every place that still tells an agent or designer to put a door at the portal or to use `doors`: rules/craftsmanship.md (ENTRANCES), rules/feature-builds.md, rules/building-review.md, rules/evidence-order.md, rules/rules-context.md, .claude/skills/redo, lib/journal/cell_features.py and lib/evidence/evidence_sheet.py output, bakeoff scenarios and checks that rely on the old door spec, and the tests. Gate: a grep for the removed names (framed, DOOR_REACH, the `doors` key, 'door at every portal') finds nothing outside tasks/done.json and history; unit tests cover entrances read from the plan, including unresolved portals. Door row is set from outside ground so doors cannot sit below it (I-017). Covers I-018 and I-017. Check: the 57-A, 40-A and 42-B checks in #145 hold after a rebuild. Acceptance also includes the old #143 check: after re-applying the specs, 0 patrol door_to_wall flags and doors at the right leaf count; the door row follows the outside ground (I-017).

tasks.title: Water bodies as features (ponds)
tasks.notes: Cause: ground leaves mapped water as terrain (ground_layer.py:170-177) and no feature plan covers a water body, so the pond is whatever the baseline left (I-014, S-018). Not verified: whether the dark basin in 48,-45 is leftover ghost baseline or an unpainted hole. Deliver: a water-body feature in the plan vocabulary with outline from the vector map or aerial, water level, bank and edge; it sits in the cell plan as a feature to build, like a building, and records its evidence and provenance the way the facade plan (#145) does. Check: the pond in 48,-45 is a planned, built feature with water at a sensible level and a defined bank, not a dark hole.

tasks.title: Pitched roofs use stairs and slabs correctly
tasks.notes: Cause: roof_pitched (feature_build.py:1687) writes slabs only and never stairs; the roof in the snag shows full stepped blocks, so first confirm which path built it (the zoned pitched path from #125 is a candidate, not verified) (I-019, S-024). Deliver: pitched roof surfaces use the stair, slab and full block of the roof material, each set by what it means in the game. Stairs: facing up-slope toward the ridge, half bottom for an ordinary slope, shape set at hips, valleys and corners (inner or outer), never used where a flat or vertical face is meant (walkable steps, own collision). Slabs: type bottom or top on purpose; a double slab is never left where a full block was meant. Ridges and eaves use the right half-blocks so the roof does not read as a staircase; waterlogged stays false. A roof material with no stair or slab variant falls back to a full block and says so, never another material (use block_family_variants to check). Tests cover a simple gable, a hip and a valley, asserting each block's state. Check: West's pitched roof reads as a slope, with stairs facing up-slope, corners shaped, and no mismatched slab halves or stray full-block terraces. Start with a spike: confirm which code path built West's roof (roof_pitched or the zoned pitched path from #125) before changing either; the flat-roof issue (I-009) is confirmed, so do not regress the ridge shape.

tasks.title: Decor read from the aerial and photos: hedges round buildings, plaza seating
tasks.notes: Cause: #127 places street furniture only where the vector map has points or barriers, so hedges round Retail and plaza seating that show in the aerial are missed (I-008, S-026). Deliver: a decor plan read from the aerial and photos (hedges and borders, seating, bike racks, bins), with each item's source and confidence, and decor built from that plan; items it cannot resolve are listed, not silently skipped. Same pattern as the facade plan (#145): reuse its provenance fields. Keep the bike-rack fences the owner accepted. Check: 48,-44 has hedges round Retail and seating in the plaza where the aerial shows them.

tasks.title: Shared provenance record for evidence-read plan items
tasks.notes: Why: #145 (facade entrances), #148 (water bodies) and #150 (decor) each say 'record source and confidence and list what is unresolved'; three private versions would drift. Deliver: one helper and schema, built on the existing decision_record evidence store (registry/evidence ids), not a new store: source (given coordinate, register entry, photo read, aerial, lidar, vector map, inference), confidence, evidence ids, and an unresolved reason; helpers to attach it to a plan item and to list a cell's unresolved items for the cell view. Check: unit tests, and #145, #148 and #150 import it and define no provenance fields of their own.

tasks.title: Issues: hold an issue for a named ticket, and take back a wrongly logged fix
tasks.notes: Cause: #128 was logged as the fix for the planning-order issue (I-007), but its check is not met until #140 lands; the issue shows fix-landed and the digest counts it as ready for review, and issues.py has no way to withdraw a fix. Deliver: `issues.py unfix I-nnn F-n --reason T` (keeps the log, marks the fix withdrawn) and `issues.py hold I-nnn --until '#140'` (digest and sync skip the issue until that ticket is done). Digest wording says how many are held. Check: I-007 stops showing as ready for review until #140 is archived.

tasks.title: Drop small disconnected footprint pieces from zoned features
tasks.notes: Cause: a zoned feature's footprint keeps every outline cell that passes the lidar-mass test (feature_build.py, zone pipeline near line 288: square, lidar-mass intersect, median, snap) and nothing removes small pieces not joined to the main building, so a one- or two-cell piece gets walls and a stone cap. Jubilee's second build has four: a 2-cell spur at (6247,-5461)+(6248,-5461) and single columns at (6260,-5479), (6242,-5473) and (6268,-5519) (I-016, S-020). Not verified: that the lidar-mass test is why they pass. Deliver: after the mass test keep only connected pieces of the footprint big enough to be a building part (a minimum cell count in a named constant) and drop the rest; list what was dropped per feature in the dry run (cell count and position) so a real small structure such as a porch can be kept by the spec. Tests: a main mass plus a 1-cell and a 2-cell piece (both dropped), and a small piece that touches the main mass (kept). Check: after Jubilee is rebuilt none of the four pieces stands in the world and the main building is unchanged. Relates to the footprint trimming in #116; independent of the facade plan (#145).
